That is the whole skeleton — it exists so you can prove the stack\nruns before you build anything on it.\n\nAdd your routes in their own modules (app/routes/posts.py and so on) and include\nthem here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import settings\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n\n    @app.get(\"/admin\")\n    def admin_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/hello.html\", {\"title\": \"Admin\"}\n        )\n\n    @app.get(\"/\")\n    def public_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"public/home.html\",\n            {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"items\": []},\n        )\n\n    # Your ticket work plugs in here, e.g.\n    #   from app.routes import posts\n    #   app.include_router(posts.router)\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n=== app/publish.py\n\"\"\"Render the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nT00 publishes a placeholder home page. As you build content types, extend\nrender_site() to write one file per published item. Two rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import settings\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — make them yours. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\nheader a { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    env = environment()\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n    (out / \"index.html\").write_text(\n        env.get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\n            title=settings.SITE_TITLE, items=[], css_path=\"style.css\",\n            home_path=\"index.html\",\n        )\n    )\n    return out\n=== app/settings.py\n\"\"\"Configuration, read from the environment (never hard-code secrets).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nTEMPLATES = ROOT / \"templates\"\nSITE = ROOT / \"site\"\n\nSECRET_KEY = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SECRET_KEY\", \"dev-only-not-for-production\")\nDATABASE_PATH = Path(os.environ.get(\"CMS_DATABASE\", ROOT / \"cms.db\"))\nSITE_TITLE = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SITE_TITLE\", \"My CMS\")\n# Set this to your Pages URL once you deploy, e.g.\n# https://yourname.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\nBASE_PATH = os.environ.get(\"CMS_BASE_PATH\", \"\")\n=== templates/admin/hello.html\n{% extends \"base.html\" %}\n{% block content %}\n  <h1>T00: hello admin</h1>\n  <p>The stack works. Now build ticket T01.</p>\n{% endblock %}\n=== templates/base.html\n<!doctype html>\n<html lang=\"en\">\n<head>\n  <meta charset=\"utf-8\">\n  <meta name=\"viewport\" content=\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\">\n  <title>{% block title %}{{ title }}{% endblock %}</title>\n  <link rel=\"stylesheet\" href=\"{{ css_path | default('style.css') }}\">\n</head>\n<body>\n  <header><a href=\"{{ home_path | default('index.html') }}\">{{ title }}</a></header>\n  <main>{% block content %}{% endblock %}</main>\n  <footer><small>IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2</small></footer>\n</body>\n</html>\n=== templates/public/home.html\n{% extends \"base.html\" %}\n{% block content %}\n  <h1>{{ title }}</h1>\n  {% if items %}\n    <ul>{% for item in items %}<li><a href=\"{{ item.href }}\">{{ item.title }}</a></li>{% endfor %}</ul>\n  {% else %}\n    <p>Nothing published yet.</p>\n  {% endif %}\n{% endblock %}\n=== tests/conftest.py\n\"\"\"Shared test fixtures.\n\n`client` gives you the app. `client_as(role)` gives you a client that is logged\nin as a seeded user of that role — it works as soon as your login route exists,\nso access-control tests stay one line:\n\n    def test_editor_cannot_manage_users(client_as):\n        assert client_as(\"editor\").get(\"/admin/users\").status_code in (302, 403)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app.main import create_app\n\n# Matches scripts/seed_demo.py. Passwords come from the environment there; in\n# tests they are fixed and meaningless.\nDEMO_USERS = {\n    \"admin\": {\"email\": \"admin@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-admin-pw\"},\n    \"editor\": {\"email\": \"editor@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-editor-pw\"},\n}\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client() -> TestClient:\n    return TestClient(create_app())\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client_as():\n    \"\"\"Return a factory: client_as(\"editor\") -> a logged-in TestClient.\"\"\"\n\n    def _login(role: str) -> TestClient:\n        user = DEMO_USERS[role]\n        c = TestClient(create_app())\n        response = c.post(\"/login\", data={\"email\": user[\"email\"],\n                                          \"password\": user[\"password\"]},\n                          follow_redirects=False)\n        if response.status_code == 404:\n            pytest.skip(\"No /login route yet — build the login ticket first.\")\n        assert response.status_code in (200, 302, 303), (\n            f\"Login as {role} failed with {response.status_code}\")\n        return c\n\n    return _login\n=== tests/test_t00.py\n\"\"\"T00: the walking skeleton. These pass in the fresh template.\n\nDo not delete them. If a change breaks them, the change broke the app's front\ndoor.\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef test_admin_console_answers(client):\n    response = client.get(\"/admin\")\n    assert response.status_code == 200\n    assert \"hello admin\" in response.text.lower()\n\n\ndef test_public_home_answers(client):\n    response = client.get(\"/\")\n    assert response.status_code == 200\n\n\ndef test_publish_writes_a_site(tmp_path):\n    from app.publish import render_site\n\n    out = render_site(tmp_path / \"site\")\n    assert (out / \"index.html\").exists() and (out / \"style.css\").exists()\n\n\ndef test_published_html_uses_relative_paths(tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"Root-absolute paths break on GitHub Pages project URLs (rubric F2).\"\"\"\n    from app.publish import render_site\n\n    html = (render_site(tmp_path / \"site\") / \"index.html\").read_text()\n    assert 'href=\"/' not in html and 'src=\"/' not in html\n=== scripts/seed_demo.py\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Create demo data so a grader (and you) can use the CMS immediately.\n\n    uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py\n\nT00 has nothing to seed. As you build content types, extend this so it creates:\n  - one admin and one editor (passwords read from .env, never hard-coded)\n  - a few posts and pages, at least one draft and one published\n\nThe rubric expects this to run clean on a fresh clone with .env.example values\n(item E4), because the database itself is never committed.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    admin_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\")\n    editor_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD\")\n    if not admin_pw or not editor_pw:\n        print(\"Set CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD and CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD in .env \"\n              \"(copy .env.example).\")\n        return 1\n\n    # TODO (your tickets): create the users, then the demo content.\n    print(\"Nothing to seed yet: no content types exist. \"\n          \"Extend scripts/seed_demo.py as you build T01+.\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n=== .env.example\n# Copy to .env (which is gitignored) and change the values.\nCMS_SECRET_KEY=change-me-to-a-long-random-string\nCMS_SITE_TITLE=Knox County Historical Society\nCMS_DATABASE=cms.db\n# Demo accounts created by scripts/seed_demo.py\nCMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=change-me-admin\nCMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD=change-me-editor\n# Set after you deploy, e.g. https://yourname.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\nCMS_BASE_PATH=\n=== .gitignore\n.env\n*.db\nsite/\n__pycache__/\n.pytest_cache/\n.venv/\n.claude/state/\n.DS_Store","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"0ac2466a-fd5c-4137-8f2a-8aeb30739cba","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"02dd2c32-7338-49d5-8a05-94b1c55dc316","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"02dd2c32-7338-49d5-8a05-94b1c55dc316","version":"2.1.299","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"1b03e980-2e04-47d1-936a-350d8346e59d","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"211e62ed-d02b-4035-826a-61e7cae1461f","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/yining/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/tdd\n\n# Test-Driven Development\n\nTDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.\n\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\n## What a good test is\n\nTests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: \"user can checkout with valid cart\" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.\n\nSee [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.\n\n## Seams: where tests go\n\nA **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.\n\n**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.\n\nAsk: \"What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?\"\n\nWhen the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with \"codebase-design\" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.\n\n## Anti-patterns\n\n- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.\n- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.\n- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.\n\n## Rules of the loop\n\n- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.\n- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.\n- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"d37d6b5e-5301-4a00-a3e2-6d0f48108258","timestamp":"2026-10-17T09:24:54.255Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01HxxJrKnfVku2kwJj8irntU","session_id":"02dd2c32-7338-49d5-8a05-94b1c55dc316","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"02dd2c32-7338-49d5-8a05-94b1c55dc316","version":"2.1.299","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

email=user[\"email\"],\n                                 password=user[\"password\"], role=role,\n                                 display_name=user[\"display_name\"])\n    return tmp_path / \"cms.db\"\n\n\ndef csrf_token(page_html: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Pull the CSRF token out of a rendered console form.\"\"\"\n    match = re.search(r'name=\"csrf_token\" value=\"([^\"]+)\"', page_html)\n    assert match, \"page has no CSRF token\"\n    return match.group(1)\n\n\ndef login(c: TestClient, email: str, password: str):\n    \"\"\"Submit the login form the way a browser does, A session is\na random id kept in the `sessions` table; the browser holds it inside a signed\ncookie (see app/web.py), so logging out deletes the row and ends the session\neven if someone kept a copy of the cookie.\n\nAnything the console should refuse raises `Refused` with a message to show.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport secrets\nimport sqlite3\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom argon2 import PasswordHasher\nfrom argon2.exceptions import VerifyMismatchError\n\n_hasher = PasswordHasher()\n\n\nclass Refused(Exception):\n    \"\"\"An account action the console refuses, with the reason to show.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, message: str) -> None:\n        super().__init__(message)\n        self.message = message\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass User:\n    id: int\n    email: str\n    role: str\n    display_name: str | None\n    state: str\n    needs_setup: bool\n\n\ndef _user(row: sqlite3.Row) -> User:\n    return User(id=row[\"id\"], email=row[\"email\"], role=row[\"role\"],\n                display_name=row[\"display_name\"], state=row[\"state\"],\n                needs_setup=bool(row[\"needs_setup\"]))\n\n\ndef _normalise_email(email: str) -> str:\n    return email.strip().lower()\n\n\ndef create_user(conn: sqlite3.Connection, *, email: str, password: str,\n                role: str, display_name: str | None = None,\n                needs_setup: bool = False) -> User:\n    cur = conn.execute(\n        \"INSERT INTO users (email, password_hash, role, display_name, needs_setup)\"\n        \" VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n        (_normalise_email(email), _hasher.hash(password), role, display_name,\n         int(needs_setup)),\n    )\n    row = conn.execute(\"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?\", (cur.lastrowid,)).fetchone()\n    return _user(row)\n\n\ndef log_in(conn: sqlite3.Connection, email: str, password: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Check the credentials and start a session. Returns the session id.\"\"\"\n    row = conn.execute(\"SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?\",\n                       (_normalise_email(email),)).fetchone()\n    try:\n        _hasher.verify(row[\"password_hash\"], password)\n    except VerifyMismatchError:\n        raise Refused(\"邮箱或密码错误。\") from None\n    session_id = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n    conn.execute(\"INSERT INTO sessions (id, user_id) VALUES (?, ?)\",\n                 (session_id, row[\"id\"]))\n    return session_id\n\n\ndef user_for_session(conn: sqlite3.Connection, session_id: str | None) -> User | None:\n    if not session_id:\n        return None\n    row = conn.execute(\n        \"SELECT users.* FROM sessions JOIN users ON users.id = sessions.user_id\"\n        \" WHERE sessions.id = ?\", (session_id,)).fetchone()\n    return _user(row) if row else None\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1230,"cache_read_input_tokens":84183,"output_tokens":1455,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":285},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1230,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1455,"cache_read_input_tokens":84183,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1230,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1230},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01T58A9Tm9H2mRqrDtZjTDsH":{"file_path":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/app/accounts.py","content":"\"\"\"Accounts: users, password hashing, login and logout, and sessions.\n\nPasswords are only ever stored as argon2 hashes and never logged. Returns the session id.\"\"\"\n    row = conn.execute(\"SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?\",\n                       (_normalise_email(email),)).fetchone()\n    try:\n        _hasher.verify(row[\"password_hash\"], password)\n    except VerifyMismatchError:\n        raise Refused(\"邮箱或密码错误。\") from None\n    session_id = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n    conn.execute(\"INSERT INTO sessions (id, user_id) VALUES (?, ?)\",\n                 (session_id, row[\"id\"]))\n    return session_id\n\n\ndef user_for_session(conn: sqlite3.Connection, session_id: str | None) -> User | None:\n    if not session_id:\n        return None\n    row = conn.execute(\n        \"SELECT users.* FROM sessions JOIN users ON users.id = sessions.user_id\"\n        \" WHERE sessions.id = ?\", (session_id,)).fetchone()\n    return _user(row) if row else None\n"}},"apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cg7ZzP4jNn9aiUJ74gvsx","requestedModel":"claude-opus-5-5","attributionSkill":"mattpocock-skills:tdd","attributionPlugin":"mattpocock-skills","type":"assistant","uuid":"32deb7dd-4e38-4852-aa22-051313606c23","timestamp":"2026-10-17T09:26:17.739Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"02dd2c32-7338-49d5-8a05-94b1c55dc316","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"02dd2c32-7338-49d5-8a05-94b1c55dc316","version":"2.1.299","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

{"parentUuid":"95f3e8bb-7f7b-4556-91b1-31f9dd1164bb","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg7a1UFZNXTP4jvLEx1PV","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_013paZrmVCgEdcqEYA2XoZwv","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/app/web.py","content":"\"\"\"Console plumbing shared by every route: templates, the signed session\ncookie, CSRF tokens, flash messages, and the signed-in guard.\n\nThe session cookie (Starlette's SessionMiddleware, signed with itsdangerous\nusing CMS_SECRET_KEY) holds only three things: the session id, the CSRF token,\nand pending flash messages. Who is signed in is decided by the `sessions`\ntable, never by the cookie alone.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport secrets\n\nfrom fastapi import Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import accounts, db, settings\n\nSESSION_COOKIE = \"cms_session\"\nSESSION_MAX_AGE = 12 * 60 * 60  # seconds; sign in again after half a day\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n\n\ndef csrf_token(request: Request) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The token every console form carries as a hidden `csrf_token` field.\"\"\"\n    token = request.session.get(\"csrf\")\n    if not token:\n        token = request.session[\"csrf\"] = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n    return token\n\n\ndef flash(request: Request, message: str, kind: str = \"success\") -> None:\n    \"\"\"Queue a message for the next page shown. kind: success | error.\"\"\"\n    request.session.setdefault(\"flash\", []).append([kind, message])\n\n\ndef pop_flashes(request: Request) -> list[list[str]]:\n    return request.session.pop(\"flash\", [])\n\n\ntemplates.env.globals[\"csrf_token\"] = csrf_token\ntemplates.env.globals[\"pop_flashes\"] = pop_flashes\n\n\ndef start_session(request: Request, session_id: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Replace the cookie's contents, so nothing from before login survives.\"\"\"\n    request.session.clear()\n    request.session[\"sid\"] = session_id\n\n\nclass LoginRequired(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Raised by `signed_in_user`; answered with a redirect to /login.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef signed_in_user(request: Request) -> accounts.User:\n    \"\"\"Dependency for every console page: the signed-in user, or to /login.\"\"\"\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        user = accounts.user_for_session(conn, request.session.get(\"sid\"))\n    if user is None:\n        raise LoginRequired\n    return user\n\n\ndef redirect(url: str) -> RedirectResponse:\n    return RedirectResponse(url, status_code=303)\n\n\nasync def login_required_handler(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> RedirectResponse:\n    return redirect(\"/login\")\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1557,"cache_read_input_tokens":85413,"output_tokens":1404,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":248},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1557,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1404,"cache_read_input_tokens":85413,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1557,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1557},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_013paZrmVCgEdcqEYA2XoZwv":{"file_path":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/app/web.py","content":"\"\"\"Console plumbing shared by every route: templates, the signed session\ncookie, CSRF tokens, flash messages, and the signed-in guard.\n\nThe session cookie (Starlette's SessionMiddleware, signed with itsdangerous\nusing CMS_SECRET_KEY) holds only three things: the session id, the CSRF token,\nand pending flash messages. Who is signed in is decided by the `sessions`\ntable, never by the cookie alone.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport secrets\n\nfrom fastapi import Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import accounts, db, settings\n\nSESSION_COOKIE = \"cms_session\"\nSESSION_MAX_AGE = 12 * 60 * 60  # seconds; Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import settings\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n\n    @app.get(\"/admin\")\n    def admin_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/hello.html\", {\"title\": \"Admin\"}\n        )\n\n    @app.get(\"/\")\n    def public_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"public/home.html\",\n            {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"items\": []},\n        )\n\n    # Your ticket work plugs in here, e.g.\n    #   from app.routes import posts\n    #   app.include_router(posts.router)\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n","userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"cdd590fb-0768-40c9-98f7-08d8e1f61a1f","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"02dd2c32-7338-49d5-8a05-94b1c55dc316","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"02dd2c32-7338-49d5-8a05-94b1c55dc316","version":"2.1.299","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

- <<'EOF'\np='tests/test_t01_login.py'\ns=open(p).read()\ns=s.replace('from fastapi.testclient import TestClient','import pytest\\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient')\ns+='''\n\ndef new_editor_needing_setup():\n    add_user(email=\"new@example.test\", password=\"temporary-pw\", role=\"editor\",\n             needs_setup=True)\n\n\ndef submit_setup(c: TestClient, display_name: str, password: str,\n                 password_confirm: str | None = None):\n    token = csrf_token(c.get(\"/admin/setup\").text)\n    return c.post(\"/admin/setup\", data={\n        \"csrf_token\": token, \"display_name\": display_name, \"password\": password,\n        \"password_confirm\": password if password_confirm is None else password_confirm,\n    }, follow_redirects=False)\n\n\ndef test_user_flagged_for_setup_must_finish_it_before_any_console_page(client):\n    new_editor_needing_setup()\n    response = login(client, \"new@example.test\", \"temporary-pw\")\n    assert response.headers[\"location\"] == \"/admin/setup\"\n\n    blocked = client.get(\"/admin/dashboard\", follow_redirects=False)\n    assert blocked.status_code == 303 and blocked.headers[\"location\"] == \"/admin/setup\"\n    setup_page = client.get(\"/admin/setup\")\n    assert setup_page.status_code == 200 and \"设置\" in setup_page.text\n\n\ndef test_finishing_setup_sets_the_display_name_and_replaces_the_temporary_password(client):\n    new_editor_needing_setup()\n    login(client, \"new@example.test\", \"temporary-pw\")\n\n    response = submit_setup(client, \"新来的up主\", \"my-own-password\")\n    assert response.headers[\"location\"] == \"/admin/dashboard\"\n    dashboard = client.get(\"/admin/dashboard\")\n    assert \"你好，新来的up主\" in dashboard.text\n    assert \"设置完成\" in dashboard.text  # the save shows a success message\n\n    fresh = TestClient(create_app())\n    assert login(fresh, \"new@example.test\", \"temporary-pw\").status_code == 401\n    assert login(fresh, \"new@example.test\", \"my-own-password\").status_code == 303\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"display_name, password, confirm, message\", [\n    (\"演示编辑\", \"my-own-password\", None, \"该昵称已被使用\"),\n    (\"新来的up主\", \"my-own-password\", \"something-else\", \"两次输入的密码不一致\"),\n    (\"新来的up主\", \"short\", None, \"密码至少需要 8 个字符\"),\n    (\"   \", \"my-own-password\", None, \"请填写昵称\"),\n    (\"new@example.test\", \"my-own-password\", None, \"昵称不能是登录邮箱\"),\n])\ndef test_setup_refuses_bad_input_with_a_message(client, display_name, password,\n                                                confirm, message):\n    new_editor_needing_setup()\n    login(client, \"new@example.test\", \"temporary-pw\")\n\n    response = submit_setup(client, display_name, password, confirm)\n    assert response.status_code == 400\n    assert message in response.text\n    still_blocked = client.get(\"/admin/dashboard\", follow_redirects=False)\n    assert still_blocked.headers[\"location\"] == \"/admin/setup\"\n'''\nopen(p,'w').write(s)\nEOF\nrtk proxy uv run pytest -q tests/test_t01_login.py 2>&1 | grep -E \"passed|failed|Error|^E \" | tail {"parentUuid":"b672878c-da4b-424b-b676-81ed8e5fc4c3","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"211e62ed-d02b-4035-826a-61e7cae1461f","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/yining/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Review uncommitted changes since HEAD (e9700f1) for ticket #2 (T01 — Admins and Editors sign in and out). Spec is issue #1."}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"719ea16e-ac2a-4114-b6b8-4d7b77ffa836","timestamp":"2026-10-17T09:31:36.596Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_013pdPUcgFFboYg2PiFtG6bY","session_id":"02dd2c32-7338-49d5-8a05-94b1c55dc316","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2","sessionId":"02dd2c32-7338-49d5-8a05-94b1c55dc316","version":"2.1.299","gitBranch":"Avulpix0412/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2"}

The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>I found no hard breaches of `CLAUDE.md`'s hard constraints. There is one real security bug and one breach of the spec's test standard. The T00 and T01 tests pass. The 14 failing tests are unrelated exercise stubs in `test_ctx_guard.py` and `test_usage_report.py` that raise `NotImplementedError`.\n\n**Security bug**\n- **Deactivating doesn't end live sessions** (`app/accounts.py` `user_for_session`, `app/web.py` `user_in_setup`). Only `log_in` checks `state`. Someone who was signed in when their account was Deactivated keeps working until the 12-hour cookie expires. Old `sessions` rows are also never cleaned up. Fix: check `state != 'deactivated'` in `user_for_session`. SECURITY-CHECKLIST #6 tests only the login, but this follows from the rule.\n\n**Documented-standard breaches**\n- **Database inspected in a test** (`tests/test_t01_login.py:171`, `stored = database.read_bytes()` with `$argon2id$`). The spec's Testing Decisions say \"Tests never inspect database rows\". This mirrors the grader's check for SECURITY-CHECKLIST #1, so it's defensible. If it stays, note the exception in the spec or in the test's docstring.\n- **Accounts created through internals** (`tests/conftest.py` `add_user` calls `accounts.create_user` directly). The docstring says it's temporary until the Users page exists, which is acceptable for now. Track replacing it.\n- **Avoid-words in test names** (judgement call). CONTEXT.md lists \"visitor\" and \"user\" as words to avoid, though it does so under Reader. The flagged names are `test_anonymous_visitor_is_sent_to_login`, `test_deactivated_user_…` and `test_user_flagged_for_setup_…`. The glossary has no word for \"account holder\", \"session\" or \"first-login setup\", so per CLAUDE.md, add those terms to CONTEXT.md instead of improvising.\n\n**Smells (all judgement calls)**\n- **Mysterious Name**: `web.user_in_setup` actually means \"signed in, whether or not setup is finished\". A name like `signed_in_user_allowing_setup` would say that. `accounts._user(row)` would read better as `_user_from_row`.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `needs_setup` branch appears four times, in `web.signed_in_user`, `auth.login` (`\"/admin/setup\" if user.needs_setup else \"/admin/dashboard\"`), `setup_form` and `setup`. A single `home_for(user)` helper would cover them.\n- **Duplicated Code**: `if not user.needs_setup: return redirect(\"/admin/dashboard\")` is copied in both setup routes. Each template context, such as `{\"title\": \"登录\", ...}` and `{\"title\": \"首次登录设置\", ...}`, is also written out twice.\n- **Duplicated Code / Data Clumps**: `DEMO_USERS` exists in two shapes, a tuple list in `scripts/seed_demo.py` and a dict in `tests/conftest.py`, kept in step only by a \"Matches…\" comment. The tests can't import the script cleanly, so this is acceptable as is.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: `role`, `state` and the flash `kind` are bare strings (`row[\"state\"] == \"deactivated\"`), with the allowed values listed only in the SQL `CHECK`. A small `StrEnum` would help once T-user-management lands.\n- **Divergent Change** (minor): `app/web.py` holds templates, sessions, CSRF, flash messages and the guards, so it will change for several unrelated reasons. Its docstring is honest about this, so it's fine for now.\n\n**Checked and fine**\n- Every POST form carries a CSRF token, checked app-wide with `compare_digest`.\n- Passwords are argon2-hashed and never logged.\n- A dummy hash keeps the timing the same for a wrong email and a wrong password.\n- The session is cleared at login, so a pre-login session can't be reused.\n- Seed passwords come from the environment, with no defaults.\n- `.claude/state/phase` is `T01`.\n- The absolute `href=\"/login\"` links are in the admin console templates only, never in published HTML, so the relative-paths rule isn't broken.\n- No dependencies were added.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>68622</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>5</tool_uses><duration_ms>68154</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>The T01 change meets every acceptance criterion as written. The full suite passes (25 tests, T00 unchanged), and I confirmed the gaps below with a TestClient probe.\n\n**(a) Missing or partial**\n\n1. **No nav bar on the setup page.** The ticket says *\"a persistent Chinese navigation bar\"* and the spec says *\"Navigation stays on every page\"*. `base.html` only draws the nav when `user` is passed to the template. `/admin/setup` never passes it, so the probe showed `&lt;nav` missing there. The login page has no nav either, which is fine because nobody is signed in yet.\n2. **A Deactivated user's open session keeps working.** The spec says *\"Deactivated users can't log in.\"* `accounts.user_for_session` never checks `state`. In the probe, an Admin signed in, was then set to Deactivated, and `/admin/dashboard` still answered 200. T01 has no way to deactivate anyone yet, so nothing breaks today. But when T06 adds deactivation and the grader runs checklist item 6 (\"Deactivates the seeded editor, then tries to log in\"), that editor's live session will still get in. The fix belongs in this module.\n\n**(b) Scope creep (small)**\n\n- Rules nobody asked for: an 8-character minimum password, a 30-character cap on Display names, and *\"昵称不能是登录邮箱\"* (the Display name can't be the login email). That last one follows the spirit of story 9 (*\"login email never shown on the public site\"*), but no spec line asks for it.\n- A `last_login_at` column and a `created_at` on sessions, which nothing reads.\n- Display names are case-sensitive: the column is `UNIQUE` with no `COLLATE NOCASE`, while email has it. In the probe, \"bob\" was accepted alongside \"Bob\". Story 8 says *\"never confuse me with another writer\"*, so whether \"bob\" and \"Bob\" count as duplicates is a decision someone should make.\n\n**(c) Implemented, but looks wrong**\n\n1. **The temporary password can be set again as the \"new\" one.** Story 5 says *\"so that the temporary password the Admin chose stops working.\"* `complete_setup` doesn't check that the new password differs from the old one. In the probe, re-entering `temporary-pw` returned 303 and setup counted as done.\n2. **`/admin` is open to anonymous visitors.** The ticket says *\"Every console page except the login page requires being signed in.\"* `/admin` returns 200 with no session. The ticket's own T00 note (*\"`/admin` still answers 'hello admin'\"*) forces this, so it's acceptable, but it's a second exception and should be written down so the checklist 5 grader doesn't flag it.\n3. **The password test reads raw database bytes.** Testing Decisions says *\"Tests never inspect database rows\"*. Reading the raw file is borderline. It is justified, though, because checklist item 1 has the grader doing exactly that.\n4. **The placeholder passwords in `.env.example` act as defaults.** The ticket says *\"There are no default passwords.\"* `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=change-me-admin` comes from before this change, but because of rubric E4, a fresh clone seeded straight from `.env.example` ends up with known passwords. The README tells the user to change them, which helps but doesn't remove the problem.\n\n**Confirmed working**\n\n- The wrong-password and unknown-email pages are identical, and timing is evened out with a dummy hash.\n- The CSRF check applies to the whole app, covers login, and a JSON POST without a token was rejected with 403.\n- Logging out deletes the session row on the server, so a replayed copy of the old cookie fails.\n- `client_as` works for both roles.\n- The seed script refuses to run unless both password variables are set, and running it twice is harmless.\n- The test isolation the spec asks for is in place: each test gets its own SQLite database through `CMS_DATABASE`.\n\nNo files were changed. The probe script is at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yining-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/02dd2c32-7338-49d5-8a05-94b1c55dc316/scratchpad/probe.py`.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>66334</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>7</tool_uses><duration_ms>69874</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

It had two axes, run by separate reviewers: **Standards** (CLAUDE.md, SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md, CONTEXT.md, the ADRs, the spec's Testing Decisions, plus the Fowler smell baseline) and **Spec** (this ticket and #1).\n\n### Fixed (each with a failing test first)\n\n| Finding | Axis | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| Deactivating an account didn't end a session it already had open | both | `user_for_session` now ignores sessions of Deactivated accounts. Test: `test_deactivating_an_account_ends_its_open_session`. |\n| The temporary password could be \"replaced\" by itself during First-login setup (story 5) | Spec | Setup refuses it with 新密码不能与临时密码相同. Added to `test_setup_refuses_bad_input_with_a_message`. |\n| The setup page had no console navigation (\"Navigation stays on every page\") | Spec | The setup page now renders the nav, showing 新账号 until a Display name is chosen. Test: `test_setup_page_keeps_the_console_navigation_and_a_way_to_log_out`. |\n| Display-name uniqueness was case-sensitive (\"Bob\" and \"bob\" could both exist; story 8) | Spec | The column is now `UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE`. Test: `test_display_names_are_unique_regardless_of_letter_case`. |\n\n### Fixed (no behaviour change)\n\n- **Test names used avoided words** (`visitor`, `user`). Renamed them to the CONTEXT.md vocabulary. Added **First-login setup** (首次登录设置) to the glossary, since there was no term for it.\n- **Unclear names.** `web.user_in_setup` is now `signed_in_user_mid_setup`, and `accounts._user` is now `_user_from_row`.\n- **The `needs_setup` redirect branch was repeated.** It now lives in one `web.home_for(user)`.\n- **`users.last_login_at` was unused** (scope creep). Removed it. T09's Users page will add it when it reads it.\n- **`.env.example` placeholder passwords** act as known passwords on a fresh clone. The rubric (E4) needs the seed to run on those values, so the seed now prints a warning when a password is still a `change-me` placeholder.\n\n### Kept, with reasons\n\n- **The argon2 test reads the database file's bytes.** This breaks \"tests never inspect database rows\", but it repeats the grader's check for SECURITY-CHECKLIST item 1, which is about what is stored. The test's docstring says so.\n- **`add_user` and `accounts.set_state` arrange accounts directly in tests.** The Users page doesn't exist until T09. Those tests should switch to it then.\n- **`/admin` answers anonymously.** The T00 tests require it. It shows only the \"hello admin\" placeholder with a login link and no console content. The real console starts at `/admin/dashboard`.\n- **The 8-character password minimum, the 30-character Display name cap, and the rule that the Display name can't be the login email.** None of these was asked for, but they're cheap. The last one follows story 9 (the login email is never public).\n- **Role and state are bare strings**, checked only by SQL `CHECK`. Revisit with a small `StrEnum` in T09, when the Users page edits them.\n- **`DEMO_USERS` is defined in both `scripts/seed_demo.py` and `tests/conftest.py`.** The tests can't import the script cleanly, and a comment ties the two together.\n- **`app/web.py` has several jobs** (templates, the session cookie, CSRF, flash messages, the signed-in guards). They're all console plumbing, and the docstring says so. Split it if it grows.\n\n### Verification\n\n- `uv run pytest`: the 28 T00 + T01 tests pass. The T00 tests are unchanged.\n- The 14 remaining failures are the course's unfinished exercises (`decide()`, `spend()`), and they failed the same way before this ticket.\n- `pyright` reports 0 errors.\n- A live smoke test on uvicorn, seeded from `.env.example`, covered login (303 to the dashboard, greeted by Display name), logout without a token (403), logout (303), and the dashboard after logout (303 to `/login`). The stored hashes are `$argon2id$`, and no plain password appeared in the server log.\nEOF\ngh issue comment 2 --body-file $S/review-comment.md","description":"Post review findings comment on issue #2"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":801,"cache_read_input_tokens":144300,"output_tokens":1776,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":801,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1776,"cache_read_input_tokens":144300,"cache_creation_input_tokens":801,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":801},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_019aRb4LouvkKxbzBpdeRL9b":{"command":"cd /Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2 && S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yining-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/02dd2c32-7338-49d5-8a05-94b1c55dc316/scratchpad && cat > $S/review-comment.md <<'EOF'\n## `/code-review` findings for T01, and how each was resolved\n\nThe review ran on the uncommitted T01 work against `e9700f1`. Those are the unfinished course exercises (`decide()` and `spend()`), and they failed the same way before I started. Pyright reports no errors; I ran it through `uvx`, so `pyproject.toml` is unchanged. I also ran the real server and checked login, the dashboard, a logout with no CSRF token (refused) and a real logout by hand.\n\n**What's built** (every acceptance criterion is met):\n- **Login and logout:** sign in with email and password. Logging out ends the session on the server, so a copied cookie stops working too.\n- **Refusals:** a wrong password and an unknown email get the same message and take the same time. Deactivated accounts see 账号已停用, and any session they already had open stops working.\n- **CSRF:** every POST in the app must carry a CSRF token, including future routes.\n- **First-login setup:** someone with a temporary password must choose a new password and a unique Display name before reaching any other console page.\n- **Console shell:** a Chinese nav bar, a message after every save, and a dashboard at `/admin/dashboard` that greets by Display name. `/admin` stays the T00 hello page.\n- **Seed and tests:** the seed script creates the Admin and Editor from the environment and refuses to run without both passwords. Each test gets its own database. `client_as()` now sends the login form's CSRF token, so it works for both roles.\n\n**Review:** I ran `/code-review` and posted the findings, with how each was handled, on issue #2 ([comment](https://github.com/Avulpix0412/iphs400-mp2-cms/issues/2#issuecomment-6232355542)). It found four real bugs, each now fixed with a test written first:\n- Deactivating someone didn't end a session they already had open.\n- Setup accepted the temporary password as the \"new\" password.\n- The setup page had no nav bar.\n- Display names that differed only in capitals, like \"Bob\" and \"bob\", were both allowed.\n\n**Things you should know:**\n- **`.env` loading:** the README now says to run commands with `uv run --env-file .env …`. Nothing in the project read `.env` before.\n- **Your local `.env` may break that:** uv rejected the unquoted `CMS_SITE_TITLE=Knox County Historical Society` line, so I added quotes in `.env.example`. I didn't open your `.env` because it holds secrets. If it still has that line unquoted, add the quotes yourself.\n- **Placeholder passwords:** the seed now prints a warning if a password is still a `change-me` placeholder.\n- **Decision for you:** I added a few rules nobody asked for: passwords of at least 8 characters, Display names of at most 30, and a Display name can't be the login email. Playground drops you straight into the admin dashboard as \"Howdy, admin\" — no login screen, no password. You're just already an admin with full edit rights over the whole site. That's the opposite of what MP2 wants: my CMS has to make you actually authenticate before you can touch anything.\n+\n+2. I poked around the checkout/coupon area (this is a WooCommerce demo, not core WordPress, so not directly one of my 7 capabilities) and found a real bug: I applied a coupon at checkout and it said \"applied\" successfully, but the price didn't actually go down. The discount logic and the UI confirmation aren't actually wired together — the interface lied about what happened. Good reminder to actually test that my own \"success\" messages correspond to something real changing in the database, not just a toast notification.\n+\n+(need 3+ more — still to do: draft vs. published visibility, page vs. post navigation placement, slug generation, Editor role restriction on Users, status filter on the post list)\n== branch's change (stat)\n notes/cms-field-notes.md | 22 ++++++++++++++++++++--\n 1 file changed, 20 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"4f3a48a1-f931-4717-92c2-ef97e5ec4a01","timestamp":"2026-10-17T11:18:23.368Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"== main's change\ndiff --git a/notes/cms-field-notes.md b/notes/cms-field-notes.md\nindex 8c4550c..a2d204b 100644\n--- a/notes/cms-field-notes.md\n+++ b/notes/cms-field-notes.md\n@@ -1,3 +1,9 @@\n # Field notes\n \n (Part 2 of the manual: at least five things you noticed inside WordPress Playground, in your own words.)\n+\n+1. {"parentUuid":"9e05797d-9c80-4258-8b07-0294aa79134d","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"109129b9-e526-47eb-9387-c6e1f1bb6ca2","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01WTr13dUUnnr8PVPvhJjUZj","type":"tool_result","content":"# Field notes — WordPress Playground, 2026-10-15\n\n1. When I was writing new posts, the advanced settings had a box called additional CSS. {"parentUuid":"b563a422-ddb7-4de3-ae49-08bbdcb5cd95","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg7ikA5Y8W1Vayem4TjQD","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01B5gi8tsgxwrEArFNnqS9S5","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yining-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/02dd2c32-7338-49d5-8a05-94b1c55dc316/scratchpad && cat > $S/pr-body.md <<'EOF'\n## T01: Admins and Editors sign in and out\n\nCloses #2. The spec is #1.\n\n### What's in it\n- **Login and logout.** Sign in with email and password; passwords are stored as argon2 hashes. Sessions live on the server, and the browser holds the session id in a signed cookie, so logging out ends the session even if someone copied the cookie.\n- **CSRF.** Every POST in the app is checked for a CSRF token.\n- **Refusals.** A wrong password and an unknown email get the same message and take the same time. Deactivated accounts see 账号已停用, and any session they already had open stops working.\n- **First-login setup.** Someone with a temporary password must choose a new password and a unique Display name before reaching any other console page. Uniqueness ignores letter case.\n- **Console shell.** A Chinese nav bar, a message after every save, and a dashboard at `/admin/dashboard` that greets by Display name. `/admin` stays the T00 hello page.\n- **Seed.** `scripts/seed_demo.py` creates one Admin and one Editor from `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` and `CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD`, and refuses to run without them.\n- **Tests.** Each test gets a fresh SQLite database through `CMS_DATABASE`. `client_as()` now submits the login form's CSRF token.\n\n### Also in this PR\n- The earlier notes and grill commits on this branch: the client brief, the field notes, the CMS vocabulary research, and the `CONTEXT.md` glossary.\n- A merge of `origin/main` that keeps both sets of WordPress Playground field notes (10 from the branch, plus the 2 from `main` as notes 11 and 12).\n- `.env.example` now quotes `CMS_SITE_TITLE`, because `uv run --env-file` rejected the unquoted value with spaces.\n\n### Verification\n- `uv run pytest`: the 28 T00 + T01 tests pass. The 14 failures that remain are the course's unfinished exercises (`decide()`, `spend()`), which failed the same way before this ticket.\n- `pyright` reports 0 errors.\n- A live smoke test on uvicorn, seeded from `.env.example`, passed.\n- The `/code-review` findings and how each was resolved are in a comment on #2.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\nEOF\ngh pr create --base main --title \"T01: Admins and Editors sign in and out\" --body-file $S/pr-body.md","description":"Open pull request to main for T01"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":649,"cache_read_input_tokens":155620,"output_tokens":1102,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":649,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1102,"cache_read_input_tokens":155620,"cache_creation_input_tokens":649,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":649},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01B5gi8tsgxwrEArFNnqS9S5":{"command":"cd /Users/yining/orca/workspaces/iphs400-mp2-cms/IPHS400-Mini-Project-2 && S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-yining-orca-workspaces-iphs400-mp2-cms-IPHS400-Mini-Project-2/02dd2c32-7338-49d5-8a05-94b1c55dc316/scratchpad && cat > $S/pr-body.md <<'EOF'\n## T01: Admins and Editors sign in and out\n\nCloses #2.
